label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, poison-message, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 8 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER idempotent (unchanged), LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS retry -> dead_letter); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: poison-message
case.title: The ledger stops booking: a poison message
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the ledger consumer that retries unreadable messages forever (BAD_EVENTS=retry), then one unreadable event from the provider (a payment.updated with its amount as a decimal string): the ledger consumer is stuck on it, and books nothing behind it.
case.remedy: roll the ledger consumer back to dead-lettering: the poison goes to the dead-letter topic, the backlog drains, and the money check passes again

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, messages up to it were not handled yet: ledger 189.

diagnosis.hypothesis: One malformed event, provider-events partition 2 offset 86, has an amount that is not positive integer cents. It arrived about 18:33:47. ledger-consumer had been redeployed at 18:33:45 with BAD_EVENTS=retry, so it retries that message forever (backoff up to 15 s) and never moves past offset 86. Booking stopped: the ledger's 'posted' count fell to 0 by 18:34:48. Later events on that partition queue behind it, so ledger lag rose from 0 to 235 and the money check cannot settle past its cutoff, which fires BooksBehindProvider. payment-confirmer (BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter) dead-lettered the same event at 18:33:47 and kept going, so only the ledger is behind. Open: the source of the bad amount (provider payload, receiver or our data), and ledger-consumer's settings before the deploy, including whether LEDGER_HANDLER changed.

evidence.shows: Consumer lag went from 0 to 1 to 235 between 18:32:51 and 18:34:51, which confirms the symptom.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 18:33:45 with BAD_EVENTS=retry. payment-confirmer runs BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter. All other services were created at 18:32:19.
ledger-consumer retries the same message, provider-events/2＠86, repeatedly (attempt 9 at 18:34:48, backoff now 15 s) with the error 'amount must be positive integer cents'.
The ledger's 'posted' rate fell to 0 by 18:34:48, while payment-confirmer kept processing and dead-lettered about one event.
payment-confirmer dead-lettered the same event, provider-events/2＠86, at 18:33:47 for the same invalid amount (trace 5a7df0d705795e4ec42fb6d08559715a).
klaxon_dead_letters_total has no series, so this metric does not show the ledger dead-lettering anything; c3 shows it is stuck retrying.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its settings from before the 18:33:45 deploy, so it stops retrying the poison event forever. The prior setting is presumably dead_letter, which would move the event aside and let the consumer drain the backlog. Then investigate offset 2＠86 (trace 5a7df0d705795e4ec42fb6d08559715a): find where the invalid amount came from, and decide whether the provider's real charge or refund needs a manual ledger entry. The money check will likely flag that event as unposted until it is repaired.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses while its container is recreated, so lag rises briefly. If the prior settings were also a retry policy, or used a different LEDGER_HANDLER, the rollback may not unblock the consumer or may change booking behavior. Dead-lettering the event leaves it unbooked: the ledger stays short by that event until someone repairs it by hand.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with the current settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, BAD_EVENTS=retry). The idempotent handler makes re-reading already-processed offsets safe.
